name: pathology of thyroid masses overview
title: Thyroid nodule workup: TSH first (low goes to a radioactive iodine scan), then ultrasound and TI-RADS size cut-offs for fine needle aspiration, then the Bethesda category sorts the nodule into benign, indeterminate follicular neoplasm, or papillary, medullary or anaplastic cancer; each column gives clues, next steps and treatment in order

root.title: Thyroid nodule: which one earns a NEEDLE, and which result earns SURGERY?
lines: most are benign · not always thyroid: parathyroid, lymph node, skin, soft tissue
cancer risk: child · male · first-degree family history · neck radiation · firm or fixed · suspicious nodes
URGENT: rapid growth · stridor · progressive dysphagia · large, fixed, firm mass

groups.title: 1 · Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) FIRST: is it LOW?
lines: LOW → radioactive iodine (RAI) scan: HOT = benign (see the THYROID FUNCTION chart) · COLD → ultrasound like the rest

pres.title: Normal or high TSH: work up in order
lines: 2 · Ultrasound + TI-RADS (Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System): fine needle aspiration (FNA) if TR5 ≥ 1 cm · TR4 ≥ 1.5 cm · TR3 ≥ 2.5 cm
• smaller: repeat ultrasound for up to 5 years, stop if stable · TR1–2: nothing
3 · FNA: the Bethesda category picks the column ↓ · never a core or open biopsy for a nodule (seeding, bleeding)

tiers.title: SUSPICIOUS or MALIGNANT (V, VI): SURGERY
lines: established or suspected cancer > 1 cm: hemithyroidectomy if low risk, total if high · node dissection if nodes

head: h
Benign nodule
multinodular goitre, cyst, Hashimoto: no atypia
clue: • cyst: clear fluid, gone after aspiration

head: h
Follicular neoplasm
adenoma or follicular carcinoma: microfollicles, scant colloid
clue: same nuclei: only INVASION of capsule or vessels decides, on the resected nodule
inv: • risk factors, ultrasound, size, life expectancy

head: h
Papillary carcinoma
85–90% · nuclear grooves, clearing, inclusions: DIAGNOSTIC on FNA
clue: a neck node may be the first sign: spreads by LYMPH
tx: Surgery, then RAI by recurrence risk

head: h
Medullary carcinoma
C cells · nests, not papillae · amyloid = calcitonin
h
Anaplastic carcinoma or lymphoma
sheets of cells, no follicles: a differentiated cancer that progressed
clue: • can't swallow · pain · lung, bone metastases
inv: 1 · Neck ultrasound + computed tomography (CT) for metastases
marker panel needs tissue · ask for a rush

panels.title: After treatment
items: ultrasound 6–12 months after, then periodically: the remaining lobe + neck nodes
biopsy a suspicious node > 8–10 mm in its smallest dimension
